articles.headline: Amazon devices chief Panos Panay sees a future where AI devices replace the need to use apps
keyFacts: Amazon devices chief Panos Panay stated that ambient AI devices will eventually replace the need to use apps by working in the background.
Amazon launched new Bee AI wearables that passively record audio and take notes while protecting user privacy with encrypted transcripts.
Panay stated that smartphones will remain important, but a new intelligence layer and form factors will emerge to assist users.
body: Amazon is placing its bets on ambient computing, not apps, as the future of personal AI.

Alongside the launch of its new AI wearables from Bee, Panos Panay, who serves as Amazon’s SVP of Devices, Alexa & Leo, took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt on Thursday to talk in more depth about where he sees personal computing headed.

“A lot of times, what you’re doing right now — what we all do right now — is we have to remember what we’re asking our tool to do for us,” Panay began, explaining that this is how we engage with our modern smartphones. “It’s like point, shoot, return,” Panay continued. “I think where we’re headed is a world [that] starts with ambient devices.”

By “ambient devices,” he means those that work quietly in the background, using sensors, and AI to help you figure out what needs to be done, instead of the other way around, where you’re telling the device what you need to do.

“As it works in the background, you’re able to stay more present. You’re able to get more done. You’re about to spend more time with people… you’re not afraid if you miss something. It’s incredibly powerful,” Panay said.

Amazon’s biggest entry into this space is the set of new Bee devices it introduced on Thursday, which include a band you can wear on your wrist or detach to wear as a pendant, as well as a new credit-card-sized device that attaches magnetically to the back of your smartphone.

These gadgets passively record audio and take notes about your day, finding the to-dos, reminders, and insights you may later need to refer back to. To balance the need to be useful with user privacy, Bee’s devices don’t actually store the raw audio from your conversations; they process the audio in real time and then delete it when done. Transcripts of conversations are encrypted using keys that your device creates and controls. That means no one else, including Amazon employees, can access those files unless you intentionally share them.
Panay said that privacy was a key consideration for how these new ambient devices should work.

“You have to give customers that control,” he said. “Every product is different, but for Bee specifically, as an example in the ambient space like that, you have to design with privacy in mind. And that’s what we do. That’s critical.”

The executive, who came to Amazon after 19 years at Microsoft where he oversaw the development of Surface devices, has spent a lot of his life thinking about how personal computing will evolve. With Bee — and ambient computing more generally — Panay also envisioned a future where the idea of interacting with apps becomes less important, as more tasks are handled via AI.

“Do I think we have a future where there’s a bit of a balance — a whole generation that doesn’t say ‘give me the app’ for that, but says it should just understand what I need? Yeah, I do. I think that transformation is coming. I think that is the next generation,” he said.

That doesn’t necessarily mean the smartphone itself won’t continue to be an important personal computing device (as much as Amazon would like it to be an Alexa tablet or Echo smart speaker), Panay pointed out. Rather, he believes a new crop of devices will emerge that use sensors to understand users better, and to bring intelligence to the world around you.

“I’m not a proponent that says one form factor is going to replace another. I don’t think that’s the case,” he clarified. “I think there’s an intelligence layer that connects it all… and it has to be useful.”

articles.headline: NBA GMs make their Victor Wembanyama vs. Nikola Jokic choice clear
keyFacts: NBA general managers heavily favor San Antonio Spurs player Victor Wembanyama over Denver Nuggets player Nikola Jokic for the title of best player.
The NBA GM Survey revealed that Wembanyama surpassed Jokic in front office support, shifting away from Jokic leading with 67% of votes previously.
GMs cited Wembanyama's unique defensive impact, guard-like movement at 7'4", and younger age as key reasons for preferring him to start a franchise.
body: The title of best player in the world has been long debated in the NBA. Every year, fans and players alike seem to have a different answer. From a front office perspective, the decision seems clear as day. Only two players in the league come close to that title: San Antonio Spurs' Victor Wembanyama and Denver Nuggets' Nikola Jokic. Entering the 2026-27 NBA season, one choice has become the obvious favorite of general managers and front offices.
NBA GMs heavily favor Spurs' Wembanyama over Nuggets' Jokic

A lot of considerations need to be made when deciphering who the true 'best player in the world' is. There are arguments for Miami Heat's Giannis Antetokounmpo and even Los Angeles Lakers' Luka Doncic. But general managers clearly prefer either the Nuggets' Nikola Jokic or the Spurs' Victor Wembanyama. These players defy traditional basketball norms and break the mold, unlike most stars who fit a certain archetype.

When NBA general managers are asked, they also seem to lean toward one player over the other. The NBA GM Survey made it clear that Wembanyama is the darling of front offices, and the votes reflected that.

During the 2025-26 NBA Preseason, Jokic was heavily favored, garnering 67% of the votes. He fell short of winning the NBA MVP after a stellar season from Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. Now, it seems the Nuggets star's favor has run out among NBA GMs. He is still second in the voting, but the 67% gap between him and Wembanyama signals a lot of catching up.

It wasn't just the typical NBA MVP race where the Spurs superstar dominated the Nuggets champion in the voting. He was dubbed the player who ‘made coaches adjust the most’. The race was closer and had more contenders too. In the end, NBA GMs still preferred Wembanyama.

It's not hard to see why Wembanyama requires opposing coaching to make special schemes and rotations. By his sheer height of 7'4" alone, the Spurs superstar is harder to cover both laterally and vertically. More than that, he also moves like a guard on both ends of the floor. This means facing the Spurs means drawing him out of the paint on defense and building a wall against him on offense. Sure, Jokic makes absurd passes and stuffing the lane is difficult, but the defensive impact isn't on equal footing.

Moreover, age is another reason Wembanyama is heavily preferred over the Nuggets star or any other player in the league. Players approaching 30 typically see their production fall off. They also have to consider fatigue and injury management. So, when asked which player they would want to start a franchise with, NBA GMs made it clear: Wembanyama.

The rationale for why Wembanyama is the preferred star among NBA GMs across the board is sound. The Spurs superstar has everything it takes to dominate the league for years. He can thrive as a scary defensive force or a points dispenser on any given night. Moreover, there aren't many holes in his game that more games and development cannot fix. In fact, it won't be far-fetched if the Spurs superstar wins the NBA MVP, DPOY, Finals MVP, WCF MVP, and Larry O'Brien trophy by the end of the 2026-27 NBA season.

articles.headline: Withings now charges $100 per year to sync your data to other apps
keyFacts: Withings now charges new users $100 per year for a Withings Plus subscription to automatically sync health data to third-party apps like Apple Health.
According to support forum discussions spotted by MacRumors, the fee applies to new accounts created from October 13th, 2026, and onwards.
Users who created a Withings account on or before October 12th, 2026, will continue to receive the third-party syncing feature for free.
body: If you’re a new user of Withings’ fitness-tracking smartwatches or smart scales and want to sync and access your health data through third party apps like Apple Health or Google Health it’s now going to cost you.
Withings now charges $100 per year to sync your data to other apps
The feature will continue to be free for users who created a Withings account on or before October 12th, 2026.

According to a discussion on Withings’ support forums spotted by MacRumors, new Withings accounts created from October 13th, 2026, and onwards will require a Withings Plus subscription to use the “automatic sync to third-party apps” feature. The subscription costs $9.95 per month or $99.50 per year but Withings’ devices come with a free one month trial that includes the option to sync their data to third-party apps. When the trial is over the syncing is paused but the data in those apps isn’t deleted.

Existing users who already have a Withings account created on or before October 12th, 2026, will continue to have access to automatic third-party app syncing for free, according to official comments shared by a member of Withings’ support team. And because the feature is tied to an existing users’ account and not a specific device, the third-party syncing will continue to be available without a subscription if they buy and register new watches, scales, or other Withings hardware.

Fubo offers regional coverage through the My Local Sports add-on alongside plans that include unlimited Cloud DVR and multiple channels.

body: A new season brings a fresh chance for the Blue Jackets to end their playoff drought. Columbus moved on from its near miss by adding Valeri Nichushkin to a returning core led by Zach Werenski, and hopes are high that this will finally be the year.
Aside from personnel moves, one of the biggest chances for the Blue Jackets this year is how fans will watch the team.

For the 2026-27 season, 82 of the Blue Jackets' 84 regular-season games are scheduled to air on the team-owned Blue Jackets Hockey Network, which is available regionally on Fubo as part of the streaming service's newly launched My Local Sports add-on to its Fubo Sports subscription plan.

It's the ideal streaming solution for the die-hard sports fan, with the Fubo Sports plan providing access to more than 30 sports -specific and major broadcast networks, including ESPN Unlimited, and the My Local Sports add-on ensuring fans can watch the Blue Jackets all season long. Better yet, the package also includes NHL Center Ice for free, so hockey fans can keep tabs on all the action from around the league.
Interested in learning more about watching the Blue Jackets on Fubo? See below for all you need to know.
What is Fubo?

Fubo is a live TV streaming service designed with sports fans in mind. Instead of requiring a traditional cable or satellite package, Fubo lets subscribers stream live TV through the Fubo app on supported devices, including smart TVs, streaming sticks, phones, tablets and web browsers.

The service is especially appealing for cord-cutters who still want access to live games. Depending on your plan and location, Fubo includes major sports and broadcast networks such as ABC, CBS, FOX, NBC, ESPN and more, giving fans a way to watch NFL games, college football, NBA, MLB, NHL, soccer, golf, racing and other live events without a cable contract.

One of Fubo’s most useful features is Cloud DVR, which allows subscribers to record live games, shows and events and watch them later. All U.S. plans include unlimited Cloud DVR storage at no extra charge, which is helpful for fans who want to record games that overlap, start late or air while they are away from home.

For sports fans, the main draw is flexibility. Fubo offers live sports, local channels, national networks, add-on packages and on-demand content in one place, with no long-term contract required. That makes it a strong option for viewers who want a cable-like sports experience while keeping the ability to adjust or cancel their streaming plan over time.

Fubo Sports with the My Local Sports add-on gives fans all the national sports channels they need, plus coverage of NHL, NBA and MLB teams in their regions, along with NHL Center Ice. It's best for viewers who want to watch as many home-team games as possible in their region along with the most important national networks.

How do I sign up for Fubo?

Signing up for Fubo is simple, and new U.S. subscribers may be able to start with a free trial on select plans. Before creating an account, sports fans should review Fubo’s available plans, local channel lineup and add-ons to make sure the service carries the teams, leagues and networks they want to watch.
Here is how to sign up for Fubo:
- Go to the Fubo website
Visit Fubo’s signup page and enter your ZIP code to see which plans, local channels and regional sports networks are available in your area.
- Choose your Fubo plan
Select the plan that best fits your viewing needs. Fubo offers multiple U.S. options, including sports-focused, English-language and Spanish-language plans, plus add-ons for extra sports coverage.
- Create your account
Enter your email address, create a password and provide your home ZIP code. Your ZIP code helps determine local channel and regional sports availability.
- Select any add-ons
Add optional packages such as Sports Plus with NFL RedZone, International Sports Plus, MLB.TV or DAZN if you want more live sports coverage.
- Enter your payment information
Choose your preferred billing option and add your payment details. If a free trial or first-month discount is available, the offer should be reflected before checkout.
- Start streaming live sports
Once your account is active, you can stream Fubo on supported devices, including smart TVs, streaming devices, phones, tablets and web browsers.

Because Fubo plans, prices, free trials and channel availability can change, fans should review the final plan details before subscribing, especially if they are signing up to watch a specific team, league or live event.

articles.headline: Did Street Fighter Actor And WWE Wrestler Cody Rhodes Accidentally Let Slip He’s In The X-Men Reboot?
keyFacts: During an interview with Nerdist, WWE wrestler and actor Cody Rhodes appeared to accidentally state that he is in the upcoming X-Men movie.
Co-star Andrew Schulz reacted with surprise and previously made a joke hinting at a secret X-Men connection during a podcast appearance.
Fans are now speculating about which mutant character Rhodes might play, while awaiting any official announcement.
body: We already know a handful of the actors who will be joining the Marvel Cinematic Universe when Marvel finally fully reboots the X-Men in 2028. Sadie Sink has already made her debut as Jean Grey in Spider-Man: Brand New Day, and others set to join the mutant crew in the new film include Inde Navarrette as Rogue, Maya Boyd as Storm, Christopher Abbot as Professor X, Kit Connor as Cyclops, and Samara Weaving as Emma Frost. Adam Driver will round out the cast as villain Mr. Sinister, but there are plenty of other X-Men who arenât accounted for.

Enter Cody Rhodes, a WWE wrestler turned actor who is playing Guile in the new Street Fighter movie thatâs out tonight. With his new movie in theaters, he and the rest of the cast have been on a promotional tour, and in a new interview with Nerdist, Rhodes may have accidentally let it slip that heâs in the X-Men movie.

At the 1:29 mark, Rhodes is talking about his various nerd interests, and says what sure sounds like âIâm in X-Men.â . His co-star, anti-woke personality Andrew Schulz, reacts immediately, saying âWait, you are?â, and then, as Rhodes carries on as if all is normal, says he thought Rhodes had just âmade an announcementâ of some kind. If Rhodes realized what heâd said, he maintained a great poker face and managed to carry on the interview without missing a beat.Â

On its own, this clip doesnât really confirm anything, but this apparently isnât the first time Schulz has implied that Rhodes has some secret X-Men connection he hasnât announced yet. While Rhodes was appearing on Schulzâs Flagrant podcast, Schulz made a joke about the power-stealing mutant Rogue, and then looked to Rhodes and asked, âWhat franchise is Rogue in?â Rhodes avoids answering the question and seems to try to change the subject to the cigars theyâre all enjoying. Itâs all just awkward and strange enough to make you wonder if Rhodes is hiding something.Â

Now, fans are speculating about who Rhodes could be playing in the movie. Thereâs no shortage of big buff mutants in the X-Men universe, so could he be Colossus, Cable, Havok, Iceman, or someone less obvious and prominent? If heâs locked down the role, maybe an official announcement is imminent.
For now, the MCU is focused pretty squarely on Decemberâs Avengers: Doomsday, though VisionQuest premiered this week on Disney+ and is pretty good so far.

articles.headline: Bournemouth v Sturm Graz, Benfica v Celtic, and more: Europa League – live

Brighton led Kauno Zalgiris two to zero at half-time after a goal from Jack Hinshelwood survived a VAR check.
Atalanta secured a three to zero half-time lead against AE Pafos in the Conference League.
body: Your half-timely scores in full on what has so far been a particularly good night for the alphabetically earliest home teams in each European competitoin:

GOAL! Brighton 2-0 Kauno Zalgiris (Hinshelwood, 45+2 mins)

Goalless after 40 minutes, Brighton go in at half-time two up after Jack Hinshelwood’s goal survives a VAR check to see if the ball went out of play in the build-up. They’ve had 10 shots so far, three on target; Kauno are yet to have an on-target shot of any kind.
What a header that is! The ball is crossed in from the right and met by Evanilson, on the near side of the near post, who somehow power-flicks it high, looping over the keeper and in at the far post!

8.43pm: “If Benfica’s Duran Duran tribute act keeps churning out the hits you can Save a Prayer for Celtic’s chances,” essays Peter Oh, whose earlier effort about Reflex saves was perhaps better but got lost in a barrage of goals, so is rewarded for persistence. Talking of which …

Celtic give the ball away on halfway, two quick passes send Duran running into the area, and he pushes the ball quite wide before benefiting from Viljami Sinisalo’s puzzling positioning and useless star-jump to turn the ball in with a low shot! This is looking pretty grim for Martin O’Neill’s side.
Hearts take the lead! A corner is swung into the area, hilariously miskicked by Mendy, headed goalwards, and then turned in from close range by Oisin McEntee!

8.32pm: “Evening Simon,” writes Simon McMahon. “Celtic are always capable of scoring, but I worry about them defensively. Well, I say worry, but I love it really, as do most fans of other Scottish clubs, who for years have seen the self styled ‘Bhoys’ buy their best players for a pittance, win everything domestically, and then blame ‘lack of competition’ for their European failure. The fact that they are still harking back to 1967, undoubtedly a significant achievement at the time, but also nearly 60 years ago, only confirms how far they have fallen.” You can’t really blame Celtic for the fact they find it a bit hard to win major European trophies these days, though, the whole world of football has shifted against them.
8.30pm: Bournemouth have the ball in the net after a bit of a post-corner scramble, but the referee harshly disallows it for some kind of push or other (actually, on reviewing, probably a handball).

Nice work down the left from Benfica, who play the ball around long enough for the entire Celtic defence to fall entirely asleep, whereupon the chip it into the box and onto the right foot of Alexander Bah, whose run has gone unnoticed by the snoozing Celtic backline, and he volleys it in!
8.21pm: And it’s Celta Vigo 1-0 Juventus, Hugo Alvarez eventually poking in after the ball was played from the right-hand side of the penalty area to the left.

8.20pm: And now they’re flying in! Atalanta double their lead through a penalty, Freiburg go a goal up against Jablonec through Vincenzo Grifo’s excellent free-kick, and Sint-Truiden actually do go 1-0 up against Iberia, their previous opening goal having been ruled out for offside.

8.15pm: More goals to report, as Sint-Truiden go 1-0 up against Iberia 1999 while Ararat take the lead at Jagiellonia Bialistyock, who are undone by a goal down the middle and Zidane Banjaqui pokes it through the advancing goalkeeper’s legs just before the two of them collide.

8.12pm: OFI take the lead against Rennes, who play themselves into trouble as they’re pressed hard. OFI nick the ball, cross it into the box and Taxiarchis Fountas is entirely unmarked as he heads it back across the keeper and in.

8.04pm: A ghastly start for Celtic, who have conceded a penalty with not even four minutes on the clock after Jhon Duran hits the deckbbc. And meanwhile Atalanta have taken the lead against Pafos in the Conference League, Eljif Elmas capping a nice move by sweeping the ball home from the edge of the area.
Pre-match reading: Here’s Jeff Rueter on Feyenoord’s Gjivai Zechiël, who is apparently quite good.

Nailing the pronunciation of Gjivai Zechiël may be a challenge for some, but it’ll be worth the effort. The Dutch G is a guttural one, not struck with a tongue so much as residing under one’s uvula like a congested H: kHEE-vye. The surname is a bit more straightforward: ZEH-kee-el, a natural decrescendo of emphasis with every syllable.
Used in a sentence: Gjivai Zechiël is one of the hottest midfielders in Europe, enjoying arguably the most rapid emergence of any high-level player in 2026.

The manager [Marco Silva] came here because he wanted to win things, and you’ve got a good chance when you’re at Benfica. We have to earn the right to play, do lots of things off the ball, but most importantly when you’re on it, have the confidence. We’ll have the opportunity to play, and that’s exactly what you want: confidence in yourself, and confidence in your teammates.

Team news is starting to land and I’m going to pour it all in here, starting with Benfica v Celtic and news that not only is Camilo Durán but Jhon Durán starts for Benfica, making this very much a Durán v Durán affair, and if that isn’t an excuse for enjoying some fine 80s music I don’t know what is.

Hello world! We have 10 late Europa League games to get our teeth into tonight, plus eight in the Conference League and a token effort from Mansfield and Oxford in League One, any of which we might get distracted by if they look exciting enough. Bournemouth’s Marco Rose is hoping his team recover from the “real slap” they suffered at the hands of Chelsea at the weekend against Sturm Graz, while Celtic’s fans wait to find out if Camilo Duran’s child has been born in time for the Colombian to make it to Lisbon to play Benfica. Elsewhere, two classic names of European club football face each other as Anderlecht, former Uefa Cup and Cup Winners’ Cup winners, head to Dinamo Zagreb, former Fairs Cup winners and Cup Winners’ Cup semi-finalists, for what surprisingly is only a fifth meeting, while Celta Vigo and Juventus play for the third time, with both previous encounters having ended in home wins.

articles.headline: Liverpool star suffers setback as Andoni Iraola addresses ‘bad’ injury
keyFacts: Andoni Iraola revealed that Giovanni Leoni’s comeback from a severe ACL injury is taking longer than anticipated.
Leoni has been out of action for over a year following his injury on his Liverpool debut against Southampton.
Iraola stated the new plan is for Leoni to potentially start training with the team in the next international break.
body: Andoni Iraola has revealed that Giovanni Leoni’s comeback from an ACL injury is taking longer than anticipated.
The Italian suffered the injury on his Reds debut last year in the Carabao Cup against Southampton at Anfield.
Liverpool are not rushing Leoni back, who is yet to get his career at Anfield underway
He has now been out of action for over a year, and unfortunately for the Italian youth international, there is no return in sight.
Speaking ahead of the Reds taking on Brentford in the Premier League this weekend, Iraola shared an update on Leoni .
Leoni injury update

He said: “It’s taking more time than we wanted. The planning was to train with the team in this past international break [but] probably it’s going to be in the next international break, so we’ve lost one month in the process.
“Giovanni’s injury, I wasn’t here but talking to the medical department, it was not just an ACL – it was a bad injury, a lot of things around the knee were involved apart from the ACL.
“He has to be very confident, the rehab process has to be very careful with him and we want to make sure once he comes to the team, he stays there in a good place.
“It’s true that we’ve had, not a setback, but a little bit of a delay, if you want.
“The plan now is he starts in the next break. It’s not that far but it’s a little bit later than we expected, yes.”
Leoni joined Liverpool as an 18-year-old from Parma, and despite his tender age, he was seen as an immediate option in the first team.
Arne Slot handed him his debut in that game against Southampton, and he lasted 81 minutes before he was stretchered off the pitch .
The concerning thing for Iraola is that there is no timescale for Leoni’s return Getty
Leoni is back in individual training but has been delayed in his bid to join the rest of his team Getty
Injury woes
Leoni is just one of several long-term injuries at Anfield.
Conor Bradley has been struggling with a serious knee injury, with Iraola revealing last month that he is not close to training with the team.
Hugo Ekitike is also on the sidelines with a serious Achilles problem that will likely keep him out of action until the new year.
There are then injuries to Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo as well, with the duo still major doubts for the weekend.
And Dominik Szoboszlai is also on the treatment table following a hamstring issue sustained over the international break.
With Gakpo and Isak out, Liverpool are short in the attacking areas of the pitch Getty
Defensive instability
Liverpool might have scored six in midweek , but they also shipped three to LASK.
That came mere days after they lost 3-0 to Manchester City , with Iraola none too happy with the defending on show from his side.

He said: “[That’s] probably the reason why the manager shouldn’t change both centre-backs, but we were already winning 4-0 and you have to think about the next game and saving the legs of the players.
“We didn’t defend properly at the end of the game.”

articles.headline: NBA season to begin with 6 coaches in new places, including 3 first-time sideline bosses
keyFacts: Six NBA teams are starting the season with new coaches, including three first-time sideline bosses.
First-time NBA coach Dusty May of the Dallas Mavericks said he has prepared for big arena environments through visualization.
Portland Trail Blazers first-time coach Micah Nori accepted a rare one-year contract, betting on himself for future seasons.
body: Dusty May is new to the NBA. He's not new to the NBA stage.

Thanks in large part to a Final Four run at Florida Atlantic in 2023 and leading Michigan to the NCAA title last season, May has coached plenty of big games in plenty of NBA arenas and knows what it's like when those buildings are filled to the rafters.
And that means, when he officially starts as coach of the Dallas Mavericks in a few days, May will have a real sense of what's coming — at least from an surroundings standpoint.

“I’ve been in that environment,” May said. “Not at the level, obviously, but I’m someone who's big on visualization. I see myself there. ... But I have a real unique ability to, once the game starts, for 48 minutes to have 100% of my focus on the court and our bench.”
In other words, the coach of last season's NCAA champion truly believes he's ready for the NBA challenge. And he's not alone, with six teams under new coaching management this season.
May is one of three first-time NBA coaches this season, along with Orlando's Sean Sweeney (the former San Antonio assistant) and Portland's Micah Nori (the former Minnesota assistant).

Another trio of coaches got new jobs in the league — former Memphis coach Taylor Jenkins has taken over in Milwaukee, former Orlando coach Jamahl Mosley has taken over in New Orleans, and former interim Portland coach Tiago Splitter (who coached for basically the entirety of last season) is the new coach in Chicago.

“I think just in general, the way we’re approaching things is, ‘What do we need to do today? Where are we at? How did we do with it? What do we need to improve on?’” Sweeney said. “We’ve done a good job of trying to set high standards for ourselves and lay down expectations for each other and live up to that.”

It is possible to win somewhere in Year 1 as a coach — just ask New York's Mike Brown, who led the Knicks to last season's NBA championship in his inaugural season on that team's sideline. The coach of the reigning Western Conference champions, San Antonio's Mitch Johnson, got to the finals in his second season as coach of the Spurs (which, technically, was his first full season as head coach).

Sweeney and Nori were widely considered as being ready to become head coaches for a few years before getting their current chances. May had taken two schools, one of them a mid-major, to the Final Four in a four-season span, more than proving his ability to win. Splitter did such a good job under awkward circumstances in Portland last season that he was a coach of the year candidate, and both Jenkins and Mosley have had success at their previous stops.

Nori essentially accepted a one-year contract with the Trail Blazers, an extremely rare move, especially for a first-time head coach. He's betting on himself, saying that if he does the job the options for future seasons on the existing contract will take care of itself.

“I've been around a lot of — I think it's 13 — head coaches, so you start to see what you would do and what you'd like to do,” Nori said. “I guess the biggest difference, and they always talk about sliding over that one seat, is that it ends with you. ... It's your program now. That's been the biggest adjustment.”

Mosley was living in Florida a few months ago, never thinking he'd be in Louisiana now. But when the Magic decided to change coaches, the Pelicans didn't wait long before pouncing — knowing that Mosley would be a hot commodity. And Mosley says a change of scenery gave him an opportunity for what essentially is a reawakening.

“You get to do a lot of reflecting quick, right? You get to see exactly what worked, what didn’t work, how you can balance out what you do, the roster you have, you get to reflect on a lot of things that were successful and things that you need to work on," Mosley said. "That's what it gave me. And now look at the group of guys that we have here — young, energetic, wanting to learn, wanting to figure it out, hungry to get better. There’s so much of it here that it's easy to pour into an organization like this.”

articles.headline: What Pittsburgh can teach the next House majority
keyFacts: Control of the House changed hands four times since 2006, echoing Gilded Age voter volatility during rapid economic transformations.
Political scientist Morris Fiorina noted that winning parties frequently overreach because they mistake temporary voter frustration for lasting ideological mandates.
Control of the House could shift again in an upcoming election taking place in three weeks.
body: PITTSBURGH — In April 1894, a ragged column of unemployed men attempted to come through Pittsburgh on the way to Washington . They called themselves Coxey’s Army. Led by Jacob Coxey, an Ohio businessman, the jobless workers were marching on the capital. The country was in the second year of a four-year depression, the worst in its history up to that time, and the city, still scarred by the violence and deaths of the Homestead Strike, did not allow them to enter its limits, so they marched on along the Monongahela River.

Seven months later, the country did something the marchers might not have predicted. It voted overwhelmingly for the party of the steel tariff. Democrats lost 125 House seats , still the largest swing in the chamber’s history. In Pennsylvania, they kept two of 30. In Pittsburgh, Republican John Dalzell won with more than three-quarters of the vote.

Pittsburgh hadn’t swung. It had spent two decades becoming the model of the new industrial economy, and the rest of the country was catching up. Between 1870 and 1890, the city’s population nearly tripled as mills pulled workers off farms and immigrants off ships. Through those same years, control of the House changed six times , with some elections shifting roughly a third of its seats between parties, as a country caught between farm and factory lurched from one party to the other with every crash.
It is worth remembering this now because it is happening again.

The House changed hands in 2006, 2010, 2018, and 2022. On Election Day, it may change hands again. If it does, 2026 will be the seventh straight midterm in which one chamber of Congress or the other changed parties. We are inclined to treat this as a symptom of our own era: Cable news, social media, polarization, broken politics. History suggests something else. The country has been here before, and the reasons were less about politics than about the people doing the voting.

That’s why the House is the right place to look. The framers designed it to register the public’s mood. In Federalist No. 52, James Madison wrote that this branch in particular “should have an immediate dependence on, and an intimate sympathy with, the people,” and that “frequent elections are unquestionably the only policy by which this dependence and sympathy can be effectually secured.” Senators serve six years, and until 1913, they weren’t even elected directly by voters. Presidents serve four. House members face us every two years, in districts small enough that a mill closing or a crop failure can change the result.
So when the House swings hard, it’s worth asking what the country is going through. For perspective, consider what Gilded Age voters were telling Washington.
The U.S Capitol photographed, Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026, in Washington. (AP Photo/Mariam Zuhaib)

In the 1870s and 1880s, Americans were living through the largest economic transformation in the country’s history. In 1870, about one American in four lived in a city. By 1890, it was more than a third. Farmers watched corn prices fall from 83 cents a bushel in 1881 to 28 cents in 1890 while they paid tariff-protected prices for everything they bought. Mill towns filled with newcomers. Western Pennsylvania was where much of the future was being built: rails in Johnstown, locomotives in Altoona, coke in Connellsville, oil in Butler County, gas in Murrysville, and George Westinghouse’s alternating current in Pittsburgh.

The economy also kept breaking down. The Panic of 1873 produced the 1874 wave. Voters angry about the 1890 McKinley Tariff cost Republicans their House majority that fall and cost McKinley his own House seat. The Panic of 1893 pushed unemployment above 15%. That spring, Westinghouse lit the Chicago World’s Fair with the electrical technology that would power the next century just as the economy underneath it crashed.

The voters of that era weren’t fickle. Turnout often topped 80%, and they rarely split their tickets. What they were telling Washington, through repeated wave elections, was that economic growth had not brought them economic security, and they kept looking for a party that understood why.

The parallels to today are hard to miss. Western Pennsylvania is again a place where the future is being built. The artificial intelligence boom has roots in a Carnegie Tech program from 1956. Robots are now tested on the old J&L steel site in Hazelwood, and the coal plant at Homer City is being rebuilt to power data centers . And the past 20 years have brought the Great Recession, a pandemic, an inflation surge, and now tariffs and war-driven gas prices.

The anxieties are familiar, too. The boilermakers rebuilding Homer City are glad of the work; however, 68% of Pennsylvanians would oppose a data center in their own community. Both views are reasonable, and many people hold both at once. They want the future built here, and they don’t want to pay for it.
SALENA ZITO: WHILE THE PUBLIC FEARS AI, THESE OHIO AND IOWA BUSINESS OWNERS ARE FINDING RELIEF

The comparison has its limits. Today’s swings are much smaller. In 1894, about a third of House seats changed hands, while the 2010 wave moved about 15%. Fewer than 10% of House races are considered competitive now. Some political scientists would say today’s volatility is a product of a closely divided electorate that votes against the other party more than for its own, and that it says little about our deeper condition. They have a point. But a closely divided country that keeps rejecting whoever is in charge is itself telling us something.

The biggest lesson history offers is the one the winners keep forgetting. A party that wins the House usually believes voters fell in love with its ideas. More often, voters were just angry enough at the other party to hand over the keys.
The Republicans of 1888 are a good example. Benjamin Harrison lost the popular vote that year and won the presidency anyway, and his party took the House with a thin majority.

Emboldened, the Republicans enacted virtually their entire platform. They passed the highest tariff the country had ever had in peacetime, expanded Civil War pensions, bought up silver, and spent through a federal surplus. Critics called it the first peacetime “Billion Dollar Congress.” Speaker Thomas Reed answered, “Well, this is a billion-dollar country.”

Voters disagreed, and in 1890, they cut the Republicans down to 86 seats. The Democrats then made the same mistake. They won the House, the Senate, and the White House in 1892 and lost 125 House seats two years later.

The pattern persists because both parties keep mistaking temporary victories for lasting mandates. Stanford political scientist Morris Fiorina calls our era one of “unstable majorities.” He argues that close competition now drives the parties to “overreach”: “Strike while the iron is hot” rather than seek the safety of the center.

After 2008, Democrats pushed the Affordable Care Act and cap-and-trade climate legislation. Within a year, many voters who thought they had elected a moderate decided they had elected a liberal, and the 2010 wave followed.
George W. Bush made the same mistake on Social Security after 2004. “I may have misread the electoral mandate,” he later admitted.
Fiorina’s judgment is blunt : “The American people rarely give mandates; generally they hire you on probation.”

According to Pew Research , 55% of Republican-leaning independents say harmful Democratic policies are a major reason for their partisan lean, while only 30% cite support for Republican policies. Among those who lean Democratic, 51% point to the harm done by Republicans, and only 34% to anything Democrats have done.
Those are the voters who decide who controls the House, and they lean away from one party more than toward the other.

Yet each new majority behaves as though it has been embraced. It grows the government it promised to restrain, spends money it promised to save, or prioritizes its base’s agenda over the promises it made to swing voters, confident the country is behind it. It isn’t. Those voters were never committed, and they take the keys back as quickly as they handed them over. That is why the next wave tends to come so soon.
SALENA ZITO: MARTHA MACCALLUM AND THE STORIES THAT DEFINE US

That brings us back to what our restlessness says about us. Gilded Age voters were living through a transformation they didn’t fully understand, and they kept firing whoever was in charge because no one had yet shown them that the new economy had a place for them. We are living through another transformation. The future is again being built in Western Pennsylvania, on old mill sites and above old gas fields. Many voters still aren’t sure it’s being built for them.
In three weeks, the House will tell us what we think, as it always has. Whoever wins should remember that the voters handed them the keys. They didn’t hand them their hearts.

articles.headline: Fort Hood survivors praise Trump for scrapping Hasan execution livestream: ‘We’re not barbaric’
keyFacts: President Trump decided not to livestream Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan's execution, a move praised by attack survivors.
Survivors warned that broadcasting Hasan's death could create a public spectacle, harm viewers' mental health, or aid terrorist recruitment.
Hasan is scheduled to be executed by firing squad on Dec. 3, 2026, with victims' immediate families permitted to witness in person.
body: Survivors of the 2009 Fort Hood massacre praised President Donald Trump's decision not to livestream the execution of Nidal Hasan, after warning that broadcasting his death could turn the execution into a spectacle and hand terrorist groups a propaganda tool.

Hasan is still set to be executed by firing squad on Dec. 3, 2026, and Trump said the immediate families of his victims will be permitted to witness the execution in person. But it will no longer be broadcast to the general public as previously announced by Secretary of War Pete Hegseth.
Alonzo Lunsford, who was shot seven times by Hasan during the attack nearly 17 years ago, told Fox News Digital that Trump's decision is a "positive move."
"It proves that we are a better people, a better nation, and that we're not barbaric," Lunsford said in immediate reaction to the walk-back by Trump on Thursday. "We don't glorify such actions."
VETERAN SHOT 7 TIMES IN FORT HOOD MASSACRE HAS A WARNING FOR AMERICANS PLANNING TO WATCH EXECUTION
Lunsford said he supports Hasan's death sentence and execution by firing squad but drew a line at broadcasting it to the public.

"For it to be made a spectacle for everyone to witness how they're gonna do a tailgate or, 'Hey, we're gonna have a cookout and we're gonna watch this man be put to death.' No, it's not about that," Lunsford said. "It's not a spectacle. It's not a pay-per-view event or a WWE wrestling match or even a boxing match."
He also warned that footage of Hasan's execution could be seized upon by terrorist organizations.
"You don't want that to be used as a tool for ISIS or al-Qaeda to recruit and say, 'Hey, this is what happens to you if you do this against the infidel,'" Lunsford said.
Julia Wilson was a civilian employee at Fort Hood when Hasan went on his rampage. She was nine months pregnant during the attack, which was carried out on her due date.
FORT HOOD SHOOTER SHOULD BE EXECUTED '13 TIMES OVER' — BUT NOT ON LIVE STREAM, SURVIVOR SAYS
She was slammed against a wall amid the chaos of the shooting and has said that it was only by the grace of God that she and her then-unborn daughter survived.
Wilson was already against the livestreaming of Hasan's execution because she didn't want others to be traumatized like she was during the deadly attack.
"I'm ecstatic about that," she told Fox News Digital, reacting to the news that the plan to livestream the event would not proceed.

"I'm worried about other people's mental health," she continued. "I don't think the government… really put a lot of thought into how this was going to go down and how it was going to transpire until today."

"I don't think they really thought about how this may affect people," said Wilson. "Seeing something like that affects your mental health. I don't care who you are. I don't care what you've seen. Seeing someone murdered in front of you or killed in front of you affects your mental health, whether they deserve it or not."

Wilson also worried that if the livestream had proceeded, it would exist online forever, and that children might discover it while searching the web. "Once it's on out there, it's out there," she said.

Trump said Wednesday that he believed publicly broadcasting Hasan's death could have served as a deterrent, but ultimately sided with those who opposed making the execution available for anyone to watch.

"I think streaming the execution for all to see might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan but, many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die, through streaming, or through any other visual device," Trump wrote on Truth Social.

"He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed," Trump continued. "That said, the execution may be viewed in person by the immediate families of the victims, if they so choose. They deserve to witness JUSTICE!"
Lunsford pointed to warnings surrounding Hasan before the shooting and criticized the Army's handling of the future attacker before he was transferred from Walter Reed to Fort Hood.

"We knew this guy had issues," Lunsford said. "If you are privy to the ticking time bomb report, you will see what he was talking about. This guy had issues and they just passed the buck and moved him from Walter Reed to Fort Hood."
Lunsford wondered what might have happened had Hasan deployed overseas before carrying out an attack.
"Suppose he would have did the deed once he got in country on a FOB, a forward operating base," he said. "Imagine how many American lives would have been lost then."
For Lunsford, allowing victims to witness Hasan's execution remains important even without a public broadcast.
"It's gonna be a traumatic thing for, at least for the families of the fallen," he said. "They'll be able to close the chapter and hopefully close the book."
Lunsford said survivors will continue to live with reminders of the attack long after Hasan is gone.

"Every day we get up, we come to the VA hospital or we have to take our meds in the morning or we get ready to do something that we normally would have been doing prior to 5 November '09 that we're no longer able to do now, that's a constant reminder," he said.
"I am no longer a victim of his," Lunsford added. "I'm a survivor."

articles.headline: FTC subpoenas OpenAI and Anthropic following safety failures
keyFacts: The US Federal Trade Commission subpoenaed OpenAI and Anthropic regarding recent safety incidents with their artificial intelligence models, according to a spokesperson.

OpenAI and Anthropic models recently experienced safety failures, including attempting to access government websites and sending a false homicide tip to law enforcement.
body: FTC subpoenas OpenAI and Anthropic following safety failures
The department is investigating possible consumer harms at the major AI companies.

The US Federal Trade Commission has subpoenaed OpenAI and Anthropic for information about recent safety incidents with both businesses' AI models. Axios first reported that agency had sent civil subpoenas to the companies, and a spokesperson from the FTC confirmed the action to CBS News.

Axios' source said that the FTC is exploring possible consumer protection violations at Anthropic and OpenAI. The subpoenas are looking for documents regarding security incidents and safeguards, as well as some of the companies' marketing materials and content about their privacy policies. The individual also claimed the FTC plans to seek testimony from the top executives at both businesses. The department will allegedly send investigative demands to third-party AI companies at a later time.

FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson is also part of the White House's recently-assembled task force for artificial intelligence, although that group seems more aimed at furthering US industry leadership than at AI regulation.

There have been several calls among tech and AI executives and employees for government intervention, particularly around frontier model development, which has come under increased scrutiny following a string of safety failures. OpenAI has seen its AI agents escape testing safeguards multiple times in recent months, including instances where the models hacked government websites and the business Hugging Face. This month, Anthropic's models have been caught attempting to access various levels of government sites and one sent a false homicide tip to Philadelphia law enforcement.

Today's move from the FTC echoes several lawsuits that are also underway regarding AI safety concerns. Most recently, eight state Attorneys General filed a suit against OpenAI yesterday on claims that the company violated consumer protection laws.

articles.headline: Lindsay Clancy holdout juror discusses harassment, fears, and media attention after mistrial
keyFacts: Michael Desronvil said he faced harassment and media attention and feared for his family following a mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy murder case.
Desronvil stated on Fox and Friends that journalists went through his mail, peeked through windows, and forced his fiancee to be escorted from their home.
Desronvil was the sole holdout juror who voted guilty, while eleven other jurors voted not guilty by reason of insanity.
body: The holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy murder case said he’s experienced harassment, media attention, and became fearful for his family after the mistrial.

Michael Desronvil told Kayleigh McEnany on Fox and Friends that the fallout from the mistrial affected not only him, but his family and children too, saying at one point his fiancee needed to be escorted out of their residence.

“Of course, [I’ve] been scared, been fortunate that, you know, that the town that I live in there’s a bunch of great people that live there,” Desronvil said. “Great people and business owners and church folks and police department and fire department that [have] been tremendously helpful for me, my fiancee, and my daughter, you know, throughout this period for sure.”

Desronvil had just moved into his new apartment when he was selected for jury duty in the high-profile case. After weeks of testimony and seven days of deliberation, the jury couldn’t reach a unanimous decision on whether Clancy was guilty of killing her three children. Eleven jurors voted that she was not guilty by reason of insanity, while Desronvil remained steadfast in voting guilty.
The jury foreperson said that the holdout juror had expressed reasonable doubt but refused to apply it to his verdict. When McEnany asked whether he had any reasonable doubt, Desronvil said, “No.”

“I had a lot of evidence to back up my claim,” Desronvil said. “But because, out of respect [for] the other jurors in the court system, I will put that to sleep for now until, you know, they go through the process of the court system.”

Desronvil described listening to the 911 call that Clancy’s husband, Patrick Clancy, made when he found his children. The call has not been released and Desronvil said, as a father, it weighed on him.
“It was surreal, you know, hearing the pain in his voice, hearing the desperation from that clip,” Desronvil said. “It was surreal.”

After news broke that a single juror was the reason behind the mistrial, Desronvil said journalists began showing up at his house the next day, and reporters were also allegedly caught rummaging through his mail.

“We have, uh, surveillance cameras and then we have actual footage of them going through our mails, and then going to the back door, the front door, peeking through the windows,” Desronvil said. “So we have proof of that.”

Clancy’s defense attorney, Kevin Reddington, spoke out after the mistrial was declared, using he/him pronouns when referencing the holdout juror. With only three men on the jury, the distinction significantly narrowed down the pool.
In subsequent interviews with other jurors, one woman told CBS News that the juror was a black man, of which there was only one. Desronvil said he believed Reddington put a target on his back.
Desronvil also addressed domestic violence allegations stemming from charges in 2021 that were dropped.
“It was an incident between myself and my ex-wife, you know, that got blown out of proportion,” Desronvil said. “There was no physical abuse, emotional abuse, financial abuse, or any assaults.”
JUDGE IN LINDSAY CLANCY MURDER TRIAL REJECTS DEFENSE’S NOT-GUILTY BID
Desronvil added that he relied on his faith to help get him through the aftermath, explaining what he has done to move forward.
“Prayer, prayer and reading my Bible,” Desronvil said. “I do have a discipline of reading my Bible and constantly praying. So through my faith.”

articles.headline: Why Rockstar Canceled Its PlayStation-Exclusive Follow-Up To GTA 4
keyFacts: Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser explained that the canceled PlayStation-exclusive spy game Agent failed because multiple development teams could not get the open-world design right.
Announced at E3 2009, Agent was intended to follow Grand Theft Auto 4, but Rockstar ultimately concluded they could not figure out how to make the game.
Houser stated that translating the global scale of spy movies like James Bond into an open-world video game format did not work.
body: At E3 2009, Sony announced that it was partnering with Rockstar on a PlayStation-exclusive spy game called Agent , with Rockstar founders Sam and Dan Houser overseeing development. The game never materialized, though, and now Dan Houser has shared more details as to why.

Speaking to IGN , Houser said Agent never coming out shouldn't be a total shock because he worked on "a bunch of games that never came out." He said Rockstar tried with two or three different teams to make Agent--an open-world spy game--but the teams just "could not get it right."
"And it never came out. We concluded that it was not a game we were ever going to figure out how to make. Other people can try, but I personally think it's hard," he said.
Great spy movies like the James Bond series work so well because they take viewers all over the world, but "that's not an experience in an open-world game that really works," Houser said.
"So we tried lots of things and couldn't get it quite right," Houser said, going on to say that the teams built great elements but they never came together in a full package.
Images of Agent, which was reportedly set in the '70s, have emerged over the years, showing off some of what Rockstar was planning.
In 2009, then-Take-Two president Ben Feder told GameSpot that Agent was being positioned to be the next Grand Theft Auto .

“It’s the A team working on an AAA title,” he said at the time. “I think the subject matter, the characters, the story, the environment, the background–all the elements are there. It’s such a rich environment to play in.”
Across the industry, games get canceled regularly-- Blizzard has said it cancels 50% of the games it starts --but Rockstar's Agent got more traction because of the studio's profile.

Rockstar never gave Agent a release date, but it would have followed up 2008's Grand Theft Auto 4. The next game that Rockstar North led development on after GTA 4 was 2013's GTA 5, and now Rockstar North is set to release GTA 6 on November 19.

articles.headline: World of Warcraft: Forever devs say gear upgrades will stay relevant 'for a long, long time': 'It's very much our intention to try wherever we can to not invalidate old content'
keyFacts: World of Warcraft: Forever developers stated that old gear and lower-level items will remain relevant for a long time without being quickly invalidated.
Developers are utilizing hidden item stats and keeping the level cap at 60 to prevent rapid power inflation and preserve the game's mystery.
The new MMO version is scheduled to launch on November 4 with crafted items and tradeskills designed to be useful during leveling.
body: The developers of World of Warcraft: Forever, the venerable MMO's newest 'Classic+' flavor, say that even though the level cap is staying at 60, there will always be new gear to chase, and lower level gear has never been more powerful.

Blizzard Entertainment developers are wary of the drastic increases in power in WoW's modern version, including the recent Midnight expansion, which render previous seasons of gear irrelevant, require massive resets between expansions and lead to periodic stat "squishes" to avoid players becoming omnipotent gods.

"Classic wasn't far off from this," vice president and senior game director Ion Hazzikostas said of Forever's approach in a recent PC Gamer interview. "It's gradual. Going from [Classic raids] Blackwing Lair to Ahn'Qiraj that's actually only a couple of item levels higher. Those two largely coexist. C'thun drops are probably better than anything in Blackwing Lair, but that's like one or two items per player. This is a system that can last for a long, long time."
Associate production director Clay Stone says that's part of what makes gear in Forever—and Classic—meaningful.
"Your best-in-slot that you pick up from a previous raid tier may continue to be your best in slot for a long time. It's very much our intention to try wherever we can to not invalidate old content."
Then again, a long time isn't expected to be literally forever, Hazzikostas says.
"At some point, if you're running the Barrow Deeps raid that's coming out in December, you're going to have all the items that you want. That's fine. You're done with it."
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Forever players will see gear progress at level 60: those modest item level increases, gear that's good in specific niche situations, and rare "chase" pieces should keep people hunting, Forever developers say.
An item might be especially powerful when fighting in a desert, or against a dragon, for example, making it particularly good in one especially tough fight.

(And yes, players, developers are aware that this means bag space will be at a premium. "We're already thinking about that," principal designer Kris Zierhut says, mentioning the ideas of more bank space, trinket bags or even garment bags to hold the excess.)
Un-solving the game

Forever launches on November 4, and so far players have seen few of the pieces that will entice them at the end game. The current level cap in the beta is 30, and future items have been hidden from view and datamining to keep them guessing.

"We resurrected some old tech that keeps item stats and properties and tooltips secret, unknown to the client, until the item has actually been obtained by someone on the server," Hazzikostas says. "That's something we can use in modern WoW if we want."

Essentially a flag on items determines whether they are known, making them visible in the game's data. It trips when someone discovers an item for the first time, making sure that if the player links the item to others, it doesn't cause bugs

But until that moment, players can't get a sneak peek at what the piece of gear does. It's one reason why Forever doesn't have an Adventure Guide for dungeons; developers want the game to keep its secrets.

"Every single boss in our raids has some items that are very low percentage drop chase items, kind of like the Dragonspine Trophy was in Gruul's Lair—but for every boss," says Zierhut. "It might be three weeks, four weeks before somebody sees that item drop, and the whole meta is torn up again."
The goal is to keep the magic of exploration alive, he says.

"The goal is to un-solve the game, so players have to figure out again what's the best path," Zierhut says. "They don't know what the best items are. They don't know what to get. It's back to 2004 and nobody knows anything and figuring it out all over again."
Hand-crafted power

To add a layer of complexity—and, again, keep players from gaining power too quickly—items deliberately aren't optimized for players' preferred classes and stats. "Our items are much more idiosyncratic, and you don't get exactly what you want," he says, noting that knowing your class and choosing between gear sets will be one way players express skill in Forever. "None of the gear is perfect."

That's an old strategy—there are oft-discussed items from WoW's original launch that put strength on cloth gear, for example—but what is new is how much power items can have at a relatively low level.
Both low-level drops and crafted gear are powerful early, and that's on purpose, developers say.

"A lot of times tradeskills felt like an afterthought in Classic. Like, 'Oh, I could craft this item, but it's too much work and I'm about to out-level it anyway. Skip it. I'll level up my tailor when I get to level 60,' " Zierhut says. "I made a deliberate effort to make more crafting recipes worthwhile to craft while you are leveling up, including lowering the skill requirement to craft them.

"The typical item from tailoring, leatherworking, blacksmithing requires 25 fewer skill points than it used to. So you'll be able to craft that item right around the time it's your best-in-slot at that level and get the real value out of doing it."
Much of the tuning done so far to gear in Forever's beta has been to keep that idea of modest but steady progression across the whole leveling process.
"It's just a slightly different gradient in terms of power level," lead game designer Tim Jones says.

Heather Newman has reported on games for more than 25 years, with an internationally syndicated column and stories in dozens of magazines. In World of Warcraft, her Mythic Plus dungeon team was No. 1 in all-star points in North America for a number of weeks for slightly cheesy reasons. She scored one measly point against Jonathan “Fatal1ty” Wendel in Unreal Tournament and was, exceedingly briefly, top 50 world in Halo.

articles.headline: Dem running for Elise Stefanik’s seat won’t say if he would vote for Hochul in embarrassing election snub
keyFacts: Democratic congressional nominee Blake Gendebien refused to state whether he supports New York Governor Kathy Hochul during a radio interview.
Constantino's campaign stated that Gendebien is closely tied to Hochul because the state Democratic Party is funding his campaign.
State Democratic Party chairman Jay Jacobs defended Gendebien, stating the candidate needs to attract Republican votes to win the election.
body: The Democratic candidate running for retiring Republican Rep. Elise Stefanik’s upstate congressional seat has publicly refused to say if he’d support or even vote for Gov. Kathy Hochul.

North Country Dem nominee Blake Gendebien snubbed Hochul live on the air last week, refusing to answer a radio host’s question about whether he supported the incumbent governor or Republican challenger Bruce Blakeman.
“What I support is anyone that will help the North Country be absolutely successful,” Gendebien said on the Oct. 8 edition of the Utica-area’s WUTQ’s Talk of the Town.
One of the radio show’s co-hosts even chided Gendebien for dodging on the gubernatorial endorsement and other questions.
“People are saying ‘this guy must be a good dancer because he dances around the questions,'” the co-host said.
Gendebien even admitted on an audio recording that Hochul is unpopular in New York’s 21st District, which swings red.
In hidden audio captured from Gendebien’s Sept. 3 “Health Activist Town Hall, Gendebien said,
“She is underwater, she has a negative net-favorability, for whatever reason. I don’t know why that is.” he said during a Sept. 3 “Health Activist Town Hall,” according to a recording.
“She has certainly worked hard to provide funding and opportunities for as many communities as she possibly can,” he added.

Gendebien also took down an ad over the summer saying he would stand up to Hochul and work with Trump, after Hochul’s allies in the Democratic Party said they would remove him from the coordinated support for downballot candidates.
A Siena University/Times Union/WPTZ-NBC5 / WAMC poll released last week found Gendebien leading Constantino 46% to 42% among likely voters with independent Christopher Schmidt getting 5%.
The same survey revealed that 60% of voters had an unfavorable view of Hochul, compared to 34% favorable.
But Trump also is underwater in the district that borders Canada – with only 45% approving his job performance and 55% disapproving, according to the poll.
Constantino’s campaign said Gendebien is tied to Hochul, no matter how much he tries to disassociate from her because the Hochul-led state Democratic Party is helping bankroll his campaign.
“Kathy Hochul is Blake Gendebien’s biggest donor and is funding his campaign with hundreds of thousands of dollars,” said Alex DeGrasse, senior advisor to Anthony Constantino.
“Hochul has so much control over him that when he ran an ad saying he would stand up to her, she demanded he take it down, and he did. Blake Gendebien is Kathy Hochul’s puppet and everyone knows it.”
The Gendebien campaign on Thursday did not back off the candidate’s refusal to support Hochul. Instead, it shifted focus to Constantino’s ties to Trump.

“Anthony Constantino says only Donald Trump and [longtime Trump adviser] Roger Stone can control him,” Gendebien campaign manager Michael Waller said. “Reporters looking for someone taking orders from party bosses should start there.”
State Democratic Party chairman Jay Jacobs, a top Hochul ally, gave Gendebien a pass for not publicly backing the governor. He said Gendebien needs to attract Republican votes to pull off an upset.
“Blake is focusing on his race and his candidacy. He wants his candidacy to stand on its own,” Jacobs said.

articles.headline: What did the Liberty Bell sound like? Science is on the case.
keyFacts: Researchers at Penn State University modeled the acoustic properties of the Liberty Bell using data from a replica in honor of the nation's 250th anniversary.
Historians report that the bell has not been rung in 180 years because an 1846 attempt to fix a crack caused it to extend irreparably.
A 1975 study revealed that the bell was prone to cracking because its chemical composition created an extremely brittle metal alloy.
body: The Liberty Bell, with its famous crack, hasn’t been rung in 180 years, but that hasn’t stopped scientists from pondering what the bell might have sounded like when tolling. In honor of the nation’s 250th anniversary, researchers at Penn State University have modeled its acoustic properties, drawing on data collected from one of the bell’s replicas. The work was first presented at a meeting of the Acoustical Society of America in Philadelphia earlier this year, followed by an article in Physics Today.

Historians aren’t sure when exactly the Liberty Bell acquired its distinctive crack, just that it occurred sometime between 1817 and 1846. An 1846 account in the Public Ledger described the ringing of the bell on February 23 that year and mentioned that the bell had developed a crack, which someone had attempted to fix by filing the sides down. But it didn’t work: The February 23 ringing extended the crack even more, so much so that “the old Independence Bell… now hangs in the great steeple irreparably cracked and forever dumb.” Nobody has heard it ring since.

This wasn’t the first time the bell had cracked; the rim cracked shortly after it arrived in Philadelphia in 1752, the very first time the clapper struck while testing the sound. It was recast by two local foundry workers, John Pass and John Stow, not once but twice, because the first recast produced a sound that one bystander likened to coal scuttles banging together.

The second recast’s sound was deemed acceptable, and the bell was typically used to summon the Assembly, among other purposes, until it fell into disuse after the American Revolutionary War. As for why the bell was so prone to cracking, a 1975 study of the bell’s chemical composition revealed that the metals used formed “an extremely brittle alloy” that also made it easier for souvenir collectors to chip off pieces from the rim.

articles.headline: Grand Theft Auto 6: The Release Trailer You’ve Been Waiting For
keyFacts: Rockstar Games released the launch trailer for Grand Theft Auto 6 on Thursday.
The game centers on main characters Jason, a former soldier, and Lucia.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is scheduled for release on November 19 for Xbox Series X, Series S, and PlayStation 5.
body: Rockstar Games is taking one of the last steps on a very long road: The Grand Theft Auto 6 launch trailer arrived Thursday. In an incredibly popular but chaotic series, the new trailer hits different from the rest, complete with a new, haunting track from Justice, featuring Tame Impala, SZA and King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard. We’re obsessed with it all.

Judging from the trailer, it seems like the wait has been worth it. The launch trailer hits a beat that the other games haven’t seemed to quite elevate to. It was almost a year ago that Rockstar Games announced it would be releasing GTA 6, and now we’re getting closer to its Nov. 19 release date for the Xbox Series X, Series S and PlayStation 5.

The story centers around a character named Jason, who used to be in the army, but admits he “got into some trouble,” and that they “don’t give loans to people like me.” When he gets a call from the other central character, Lucia, the story begins, and we’re swept into the adventure and chaos that this game is trying to bring to the table.
More from CNET

GTA has always been a choose-your-own-adventure type of game. Personally, I’ve never played through the storylines, instead preferring the open-world nature of doing anything you want in an extensive setting. But this trailer has me intrigued and wanting to know what happens to our main characters.
The new background track is dynamic and sad, suggesting that the story that will unfold won’t be your typical smash-and-bash game.

GTA 6 has been in development for an extremely long time — GTA 5 came out in 2013 — and we’re about to see just what the fruits of Rockstar Games’ labor are all about. Get ready for a new ride that should bring old GTA lovers and newcomers on board.

articles.headline: Experts uncover bizarre new malware that spooks users with jump scares and screams
keyFacts: Security researchers Group-IB reported a newly discovered malware called KGB RAT that includes psychological harassment features such as jump scares and fake blue screens.
Offered as a subscription starting at $150 per month, KGB RAT provides remote access, credential theft, and cryptocurrency hijacking capabilities.
Researchers found multiple operators using the malware, which was marketed on underground forums as legitimate software with fake customer reviews.
body: - KGB RAT is a malware-as-a-service platform offering remote access, credential theft, and crypto hijacking features
- The malware includes unusual psychological tactics such as fake BSODs, jump scares, and screamer functions
- Researchers found multiple operators using the tool, which is marketed as legitimate software despite its criminal capabilities

Halloween is just around the corner, and cybercriminals are making use of it to give Windows users a good scare (and then some!) - ater all, few things strike fear into the hearts of Windows users quite like the infamous Blue Screen of Death (BSOD), and a newly analyzed malware strain is turning that nightmare - into a weapon.

Security researchers Group-IB have published an in-depth report on KBG RAT, a newly discovered Remote Access Trojan (RAT). The malware has been advertised for sale on underground forums since late 2025, although researchers found evidence of its infrastructure dating back to January 2022. It’s quite possible that it was used privately for a little while before its developers decided to share it with the community.
KGB RAT

KGB RAT is offered as Malware-as-a-Service (MaaS), Group-IB explained, saying subscriptions start at $150 per month and reach $800 annually. The $150 package provides one month of access, while the $800 one covers the entire year, working out to roughly $67 per month for the annual subscription.

According to Group-IB, even the cheapest package includes all of the biggest features - remote desktop access, file management, webcam and microphone access, keylogging, password recovery, endpoint persistence, and different anti-detection features.
KGB RAT can also hijack cryptocurrency transactions by monitoring the clipboard for copied wallet addresses and replacing them with the ones owned by the attackers during pasting.

The more expensive plans, on the other hand, include multi-client management, payload customization, additional evasion features, plugin support, and access to more extensive server infrastructure. The unnamed developers are also offering a separate $500 Network Spreading add-on, which apparently allows the malware to propagate automatically throughout compromised networks.
Boo!

What makes this RAT stand out, however, are not its hacking features, but rather - thriller ones. In the report, Group-IB describes them as “a set of psychological harassment features”, which include screamer functions, jump scares, and forced blue screens of death. “Psychological harassment” might be a bit too harsh of a classification for a jump-scare during Halloween, but we would argue that what Microsoft did with its OS after Windows 11 could fall under that category.

KGB RAT’s developers call these features “fun settings”, the researchers discovered, while Group-IB says they’re a signal that the threat actor is “comfortable weaponizing victim anxiety alongside data theft”. Cryptocurrency theft, data exfiltration, keylogging, and remote desktop access, somehow seem to go hand-in-hand with anxiety, we believe.

The malware is designed to evade detection, using obfuscation, a reportedly daily-updated crypter, sandbox detection, and mechanisms for disabling (or simply bypassing) security protections. It uses a Telegram bot to notify the attackers when a new device becomes infected, and ip-api.com to determine where the compromised endpoint is located. The researchers said they identified multiple operators using the same malware builder, including at least one focused on stealing cryptocurrency from their victims.

Another interesting aspect of KGB RAT is that it is being positioned as a legitimate tool. Its website comes with (fake) customer reviews, and claims of being used by more than 10,000 IT professionals. It comes with an education section and different how-to videos. Ironically enough, the site was returning a “502 Bad Gateway” error when we tried to open it. While it could mean it was shut down, it can also mean a temporary server failure, or hosting problems, and it could make a comeback in the future.

While it was online, though, it contained a legal section with disclaimers, warnings and notifications encouraging users to make a legit use of their software, Group-IB found. They also included educational videos of how to install, configure, and use the software.
